Question ID: ENG1_U04_L07_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.W.03

Prompt: Source finding: Some students with quiet study access reported fewer homework distractions. Which publication-ready sentence is most accurate?

answer.text: A. Quiet rooms always make every student finish all homework.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This exaggerates the source finding and is not publication-ready.

answer.text: B. Quiet rooms are perfect for everybody forever.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is exaggerated and not source-based.

answer.text: C. Homework and rooms are school things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague and does not communicate the source finding.

answer.text: D. A student survey suggests that quiet study access may reduce homework distractions for some students.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the finding accurate and avoids exaggeration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L07_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03

Prompt: Audience: ninth-grade students. Topic: online calendars. Which heading best fits?

answer.text: A. How Online Calendars Help Students Track Due Dates.

feedback.text: Correct. This heading is clear, specific, and useful for the audience.

answer.text: B. Calendar Stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This heading is vague and informal for a student-facing publication.

answer.text: C. A Long History of Paper Planners.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not match the online calendar topic.

answer.text: D. Things You Might Know.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not guide the reader.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L07_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.RS.01

Prompt: Which checklist item best protects source accuracy before publication?

answer.text: A. Make sure the colors are bright.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color choice does not protect research accuracy.

answer.text: B. Check that each source finding is stated without exaggeration.

feedback.text: Correct. Publication-ready work must preserve source meaning accurately.

answer.text: C. Make sure the title is large.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A large title does not verify source information.

answer.text: D. Remove all source references.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Removing source context weakens source-based communication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L07_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03

Prompt: Which product choice best fits a student audience that needs quick information?

answer.text: A. A dense page with no headings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is hard for students to scan.

answer.text: B. A one-page digital summary with headings and brief source-based explanations.

feedback.text: Correct. This format supports readability and audience fit.

answer.text: C. A private draft no reader can access.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A publication must be prepared for an audience.

answer.text: D. A random list of copied facts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Source-based publication needs organization and accuracy.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG1_U04_L07_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01

Prompt: Which sentence is publication-ready?

answer.text: A. The source say calendars helps students.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The sentence has grammar errors that make it unready for publication.

answer.text: B. Calendar thing helps kids do stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

answer.text: C. The source suggests that online calendars may help students track due dates.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses standard English and accurate source language.

answer.text: D. Students tracks due dates good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not standard English.
